non_clean.defect: 1. techniques[] maps T1567.002 (Exfiltration to Cloud Storage) but neither the body nor either cited source describes exfiltration to a cloud-storage service — the body states 'Nothing in the reporting identifies the initial-access vector' and the only described attacker action is leak-site publication. 2. The summary asserts 'multi-year student exam results running to 2026'; the cited source attributes 'plusieurs années, jusqu'en 2026' to 'des milliers de documents' generally, not specifically to exam results. 3. The summary states IFAGE 'has filed a criminal complaint'; the source says only that the attack 'fait l'objet d'une plainte pénale' without naming the complainant.

1. cves[] records CVE-2026-62415 as `type: rce`; the discloser's own page states the opposite for shipped defaults — the impact is anonymous file writes constrained to image/document types, and it 'rises to unauthenticated remote code execution only on a site whose allowed file types have been widened to include an executable type'. 2. The summary states 'The mySites.guru research campaign against Joomla third-party extensions produced six further disclosures between 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-23' and the body frames the batch as 'the same research campaign continuing'; the Membership Pro page says explicitly 'We did not discover or report the Membership Pro flaw.' 3. sourcing_note states 'Scores are CVSS 4.0' — CVE-2026-62415's 9.1 is CVSS 3.1 per the same page ('9.1 critical (CVSS 3.1, AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/C:H/I:H/A:N)') — and states 'Events Booking carries none' while cves[].cvss is null, though the discloser assesses CVE-2026-63047 at CVSS 4.0 8.7 (only the Joomla CNA published no score).

cves[].cvss carries '5.9', a figure the cited per-CVE authority does not display: the Fortinet PSIRT page FG-IR-25-934 shows 'CVSSv3 Score 5.3' and 'Severity Medium', and no cited source in the entry states 5.9. The entry's sourcing_note discloses the divergence and derives 5.9 as the base score behind the advisory's hyperlinked vector, but the base figure itself is attributed to Fortinet-as-CNA without a source record carrying it. Everything else — affected/fixed version table, virtual patch FMWP 26.033, all four evidence quotes, the 'Known Exploited: No' vendor-field staleness, and the CISA KEV addition on 2026-07-27 — verified exactly.

The entry frames the Searchlight Cyber GPT-5.6 WordPress WP2Shell case as AI "rediscovering and weaponising the already-patched" pre-auth chain (headline: "an LLM rebuilt a patched exploit chain for ~$25"; body: "tasking GPT-5.6 with autonomously rediscovering and weaponising the already-patched WordPress 'WP2Shell' pre-auth chain"), but the cited Searchlight Cyber source states the opposite trajectory: GPT-5.6 made an ORIGINAL discovery of an unpatched pre-auth RCE, and the researcher "held off on publishing this issue to give defenders a chance to upgrade their WordPress instances over the weekend" -- i.e. the vulnerability was not yet patched when the AI found it; Searchlight delayed disclosure until a fix was available. The article never uses "rediscover," "already patched," or "already known," and explicitly frames the find as novel ("I didn't quite believe this at first, as WordPress ... hadn't had any meaningful pre-auth vulnerabilities this decade").

The body asserts three distinct vulnerability claims -- "unauthenticated SQL injection and order-forgery in EasyStore" and "an invoice IDOR in Events Booking" -- with NO inline citation attached to the sentence, and neither product has a corresponding record in frontmatter `sources[]` (only the two Gridbox/Membership-Pro mySites.guru URLs are listed). The underlying facts are real and independently confirmable (mySites.guru did publish both disclosures), but the entry does not cite them anywhere, violating the inline-citation requirement. Additionally `affected_products[]` lists only "Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla" even though the body discusses four distinct products (Gridbox, Membership Pro, EasyStore, Events Booking).

Body states "anyone running internet-facing nginx should complete the F5 out-of-band patch before that window closes in early August," but the entry's sole cited source for the nginx item (cyberstan.co.uk, 2026-07-19) describes the fix as "scheduled for the F5 Security Advisory on 15 July 2026" -- i.e. a regular/planned release, not an emergency out-of-band one -- and never uses the phrase "out-of-band." The underlying fact that F5 did in fact ship this as an out-of-band update is independently true (corroborated by BleepingComputer and others) but is not supported by the page actually cited in this entry.

The frontmatter `summary` asserts the coordinated attack affected "programmable logic controllers and cellular-connected equipment at water towers and lift stations"; no cited source establishes PLC involvement in the Minnesota event, and the same summary two sentences later, the body, and the sourcing_note all say the opposite ("it is unclear whether the PLC vector ... was involved", "no source names any controller model involved in the Minnesota event"). Only the cellular-equipment half is sourced (Plymouth).

`classification.credibility: 1` overstates the corroboration the entry actually shows. The only two sources are HashiCorp's own bulletin and BSI CERT-Bund's republication of that same bulletin; the entry's own body describes BSI as having "surfaced the bulletin the following day". One assessor, two publishers — the pipeline's own Airflow entry from the same window reasons this identical shape to credibility 2 and states the rule explicitly. All three CVSS scores (8.6 / 8.9 / 10.0) and the 0.3.0→<1.1.0 vs 0.2.1–1.0.0 range discrepancy were verified correct against HashiCorp's own CNA records; the truth surface of this entry is sound.

The Hugging Face scope statement is presented inside quotation marks as verbatim but is not a contiguous substring of the cited post-mortem, and the rewording drops Hugging Face's own hedge. The entry renders it as "the only customer content accessed was the set of ExploitGym/CyberGym challenge solutions stored in five datasets"; Hugging Face wrote that the five datasets' "names and files suggest a connection to" those challenges and solutions. A suggestive identification is presented as a definite one, and the leading clause "while the intrusion did reach Hugging Face's internal infrastructure," is not visible in the source text.

`classification.credibility: 1` overstates the corroboration present. The only primary is Broadcom's own VMSA-2026-0006; the three corroborating sources (NCSC-CH, NCSC-NL, BSI CERT-Bund) are national-CERT restatements of that advisory, which the entry's own sourcing_note concedes ("rather than from its prose summary or from any national-CERT restatement"). No second party independently assessed these five flaws. Every score, version string, workaround field and credit line was verified correct against Broadcom's response matrix, so the truth surface of this entry is sound.

techniques[] includes T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) but neither cited source (The Record, SOCRadar) describes an exploitation vector for the confirmed DfE portal breach -- The Record only reports the portals "were impacted" without stating how access was obtained, so the technique is unsupported by the body's own citations.

evidence[] quote "We assess with medium confidence that the same threat actor is behind both backdoors..." is not a contiguous verbatim substring of the Kaspersky Securelist page: the source's actual sentence reads "We assess with medium confidence that the same actor is behind both backdoors, and that they are Chinese-speaking." (no word "threat" before "actor" in that sentence -- "threat actor" appears only in the preceding, separate sentence). The word "threat" was spliced in from an adjacent sentence.

1. evidence[] quote "Across all the exploitation attempts, both autonomous and manual, Unit 42 was only able to confirm three targets were successfully exploited." is not a real Unit 42 sentence -- the source's actual sentence is "Across all the exploitation attempts, both autonomous and manual, Unit 42 confirmed data exfiltration from three Citrix NetScaler targets (CVE-2026-3055) and command execution on 11 Marimo notebook endpoints (CVE-2026-39987)." The entry's quote drops the 11 confirmed Marimo (CVE-2026-39987) compromises entirely and fabricates wording ("was only able to confirm three targets") that does not appear on the page. 2. Consequently the entry's headline/summary framing ("the three confirmed compromises came from the operator's own manual work against Citrix NetScaler") understates Unit 42's own confirmed-compromise count: Unit 42's CVE table separately lists CVE-2026-39987 (Marimo Notebook) as "Active exploitation, command execution confirmed" for 11 endpoints, so total confirmed compromises per the source is at least 14, not 3. The entry's sourcing_note acknowledges an "unresolved tension" between Unit 42's narrative and its CVE table but this does not excuse quoting a fabricated sentence or leading with the narrower, lower number as the entry's headline claim.
